correlation.definition: A mutual relationship or connection between two or more things
sentences: The epidemiologist found a strong statistical correlation between smoking habits and heart disease, though establishing direct causation required further clinical studies.
Economists noticed an unexpected correlation between rising interest rates and consumer spending, which contradicted several traditional financial models of market behavior.
correlation.mnemonic: Co-relation : deux variables reliées qui évoluent ensemble.

corroborate.definition: To confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding
sentences: Multiple eyewitness accounts helped corroborate the journalist's report, proving beyond any reasonable doubt that the local factory had illegally dumped hazardous waste.
The defense attorney produced hotel receipts and security footage to corroborate her client's alibi during the exact hours when the burglary occurred.
corroborate.mnemonic: Corroborer = rendre robuste (du latin robur, chêne/force) : apporter des preuves solides.

cosmopolitan.definition: Familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures
sentences: With its multilingual residents, global culinary scene, and international art galleries, London remains one of the most vibrant cosmopolitan capitals on earth.
Having spent his childhood across three continents, the diplomat developed an effortlessly cosmopolitan worldview that helped him ease diplomatic tensions worldwide.
cosmopolitan.mnemonic: Cosmos (monde) + polites (citoyen) : citoyen du monde entier.

credible.definition: Able to be believed; convincing and trustworthy
sentences: Because the whistleblower provided authentic internal emails and financial ledgers, investigators treated his accusations against the pharmaceutical giant as highly credible.
Without credible scientific data to back up their ambitious marketing claims, the startup failed to convince skeptical investors during the funding pitch.
credible.mnemonic: Credo en latin = croire ; ce qui est crédible mérite notre confiance.

crescendo.definition: A gradual increase in loudness, intensity, or force; a climax
sentences: Public outrage reached a furious crescendo when leaked documents revealed that cabinet ministers had lied about public spending during the national crisis.
The symphony built toward an exhilarating crescendo of brass and percussion, bringing the spellbound audience instantly to its feet in roaring applause.
crescendo.mnemonic: Terme musical italien : du latin crescere (croître), une montée progressive en intensité.

culmination.definition: The highest or climatic point of something, reached after long effort
sentences: Winning the Nobel Prize in physics marked the proud culmination of thirty years of tireless laboratory research into quantum computing architectures.
The signing of the peace treaty was the historic culmination of marathon diplomatic sessions that lasted through several sleepless nights in Geneva.
culmination.mnemonic: Culmination = point où l'on culmine ; le sommet atteint après de longs efforts.

cynical.definition: Believing that people are motivated solely by self-interest; distrustful of sincerity
cynical.definitionFr: cynique, désabusé sur la nature humaine
sentences: Years of political scandals had made the veteran reporter cynical, leading him to doubt every grand promise made by campaigning candidates.
Dismissing the billionaire's charitable donation as a cynical public relations maneuver, activists questioned why he paid so little in corporate taxes.
cynical.mnemonic: Cynique ≠ insensible : celui qui pense que tout le monde n'agit que par intérêt personnel.

debacle.definition: A sudden and disastrous failure or collapse; a complete fiasco
sentences: The product launch turned into a public relations debacle when the new smartphone software crashed repeatedly during the televised live demonstration.
Following the humiliating military debacle at the frontier, several high-ranking generals were forced to resign their commands in utter disgrace.
debacle.mnemonic: En français comme en anglais : la rupture brutale qui emporte tout.

decadent.definition: Characterized by or reflecting moral decay, self-indulgence, or excessive luxury
sentences: Critics condemned the lavish royal banquet as an offensively decadent display of wealth while ordinary citizens were struggling to afford basic groceries.
The empire entered a decadent era of corrupt governance and extravagant pleasures, neglecting the military defenses that had once guaranteed its survival.
decadent.mnemonic: Décadence = déclin moral sous le poids du luxe et des plaisirs excessifs.

decipher.definition: To convert code into normal text; to succeed in understanding something obscure
sentences: Historians worked for decades to decipher the ancient inscriptions carved on the stone tablet, finally revealing details about an extinct civilization.
The pharmacist took several minutes to decipher the doctor's messy handwriting before safely dispensing the critical prescription to the elderly patient.
decipher.mnemonic: Dé-chiffrer : transformer un code chiffré en texte clair et compréhensible.

decisive.definition: Settling an issue convincingly; having the power to make quick, firm decisions
sentences: Her decisive intervention during the board meeting resolved the stalemate, allowing the company to finalize its merger before the regulatory deadline.
The general launched a decisive counterattack that broke enemy lines and brought a swift conclusion to the prolonged border conflict.
decisive.mnemonic: Décisif : qui tranche (comme une décision nette) et met fin au doute.

decorum.definition: Behavior in keeping with good taste, propriety, and social etiquette
sentences: The strict judge demanded strict decorum in his courtroom, promptly threatening to hold anyone who shouted or interrupted in contempt.
Even during heated diplomatic disagreements, ambassadorial decorum required both envoys to maintain an unfailingly polite and formal demeanor toward each other.
decorum.mnemonic: Decorum = décorum / décence : respect des formes et des convenances sociales.

decree.definition: An official order or decision issued by a legal authority
sentences: The king issued an emergency decree that imposed heavy taxes on foreign luxury goods to finance his ambitious naval construction program.
Human rights organizations protested the presidential decree, warning that banning peaceful public protests violated the nation's democratic constitution.
decree.mnemonic: Un décret impose une loi ou une règle par autorité souveraine.

deference.definition: Humble submission and respect shown toward someone or their authority
sentences: Out of deference to the visiting scholar's profound expertise, the junior researchers listened in absolute silence to his lengthy opening remarks.
The village council showed immense deference to tribal elders, refusing to pass any community ordinance without their formal prior blessing.
deference.mnemonic: Avoir de la déférence = déférer à l'autorité de quelqu'un par profond respect.

defy.definition: To openly resist or refuse to obey; to challenge boldly
sentences: Brave civil rights activists chose to defy unjust segregation laws, staging peaceful sit-ins despite facing verbal abuse and threats of arrest.
The mountaineers continued to defy the blizzard and steep icy slopes, determined to reach the summit before their oxygen supplies expired.
defy.mnemonic: Défier l'autorité ou braver un danger : refuser ouvertement d'obéir.

deleterious.definition: Causing harm, damage, or injury, often in a subtle way
sentences: Chronic sleep deprivation has a deleterious impact on cognitive performance, severely impairing memory retention, reaction time, and emotional stability.
Environmental scientists warned that the factory's untreated chemical runoff would have deleterious consequences for the surrounding freshwater ecosystem.
deleterious.mnemonic: Délétère = comme un gaz toxique qui détruit la santé lentement et silencieusement.

deplorable.definition: Deserving strong condemnation; shockingly bad in quality or condition
sentences: Inspectors discovered deplorable living conditions inside the neglected orphanage, where children lacked clean drinking water and warm winter clothing.
The prime minister described the mob's violent attack on peaceful protesters as a deplorable assault against the core tenets of democracy.
deplorable.mnemonic: Déplorable : tellement lamentable que l'on ne peut que le déplorer et le condamner.

derive.definition: To obtain or receive something from a specific source or origin
sentences: Many modern pharmaceuticals derive from active compounds originally found in rare tropical plants that indigenous healers had used for centuries.
She seemed to derive immense satisfaction from mentoring underprivileged students, dedicating her weekend mornings to tutoring them in advanced calculus.
derive.mnemonic: Dériver : prendre sa source dans quelque chose, comme une rivière qui s'écoule.

detrimental.definition: Tending to cause harm, injury, or disadvantage
sentences: Skipping breakfast on exam days can be highly detrimental to academic performance, as low blood sugar undermines concentration and mental stamina.
The sudden departure of senior software architects proved detrimental to the tech startup, delaying the product release by nearly six months.
detrimental.mnemonic: Au détriment de : ce qui cause du tort et pénalise autrui.

dictator.definition: A ruler with total power over a country, typically obtained by force
sentences: The ruthless dictator suppressed all independent newspapers and imprisoned political dissidents in a desperate bid to maintain his grip on power.
After decades of suffering under an oppressive dictator, the citizens celebrated in the streets when the military regime was finally overthrown.
dictator.mnemonic: Celui qui dicte sa loi sans partage ni contre-pouvoir.

digression.definition: A temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing
digression.definitionFr: digression, écart par rapport au sujet
sentences: The professor entertained the lecture hall with an amusing digression about his graduate school days before returning to quantum mechanics.
While the author's philosophical digression was elegantly written, it slowed down the pace of the mystery novel and confused many readers.
digression.mnemonic: Di-gresser = s'éloigner du chemin principal (du latin gradi, marcher).

diligent.definition: Showing persistent care and conscientious effort in one's work or duties
sentences: Thanks to her diligent research and meticulous fact-checking, the investigative reporter uncovered financial fraud that had eluded regulators for years.
Only through diligent study and countless practice exams did he manage to improve his standardized test score by over twenty percentile points.
diligent.mnemonic: Diligent : plein de zèle et d'assiduité dans son travail.

diminish.definition: To make or become smaller, less, or less important
sentences: The candidate's refusal to release his tax returns did not diminish public curiosity; instead, it fueled further skepticism among undecided voters.
Years of neglect did little to diminish the architectural beauty of the historic palace, whose intricate stone facade still commanded admiration.
diminish.mnemonic: Diminuer : rendre plus mince, plus petit, amoindrir.

diplomacy.definition: The profession of managing international relations; skill in dealing with people tactfully
sentences: Through patient diplomacy and multilateral negotiations, the seasoned ambassador averted what could have easily escalated into an armed border clash.
Handling sensitive boardroom rivalries required exceptional diplomacy, as the chief executive had to reconcile conflicting egos without alienating key founders.
diplomacy.mnemonic: Diplomate : négocier avec tact pour éviter les conflits.

discerning.definition: Having or showing good judgment and acute perception
sentences: A discerning art critic can immediately distinguish between an authentic masterpiece and a clever forgery by examining subtle brushstroke techniques.
The boutique winery caters to discerning consumers who appreciate organic farming methods and are willing to pay for exceptional vintage bottles.
discerning.mnemonic: Discerner = séparer le bon grain de l'ivraie avec clairvoyance.

discredit.definition: To harm the good reputation of; to cause to seem untrue
sentences: Opponents launched a coordinated smear campaign to discredit the reformer, fabricating sensational allegations about her private financial transactions.
Rigorous laboratory testing quickly served to discredit the pseudoscientific theory, proving that the miracle supplement provided zero medical benefits.
discredit.mnemonic: Dis-créditer : enlever le crédit ou la confiance accordée à quelqu'un.

disdain.definition: The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of consideration or respect
sentences: The aristocratic snob treated service staff with open disdain, never bothering to thank the waiters who poured his expensive wine.
She felt utter disdain for politicians who abandoned their stated principles simply to secure campaign funding from corporate interest groups.
disdain.mnemonic: Dédain = dédaigner : regarder de haut avec mépris.

disenchant.definition: To free from an illusion or false belief; to disappoint
sentences: Widespread bureaucratic corruption helped disenchant young voters, convincing them that traditional political parties could never deliver meaningful social reforms.
Working behind the scenes at the luxury fashion house quickly disenchanted the intern, shattering all her glamorous romantic illusions about haute couture.
disenchant.mnemonic: Dés-enchanter : rompre le charme ou l'enchantement trompeur.

disillusion.definition: To disappoint someone by breaking their naive or false illusions
sentences: The reality of grueling eighteen-hour shifts will quickly disillusion any medical student who entered residency expecting an easy, prestigious lifestyle.
Witnessing the brutal commercial exploitation of the music industry disillusioned the idealistic singer, pushing him toward releasing albums independently.
disillusion.mnemonic: Dés-illusion : enlever les illusions et ramener à la dure réalité.

disparate.definition: Fundamentally distinct or different in kind; not allowing comparison
sentences: The researcher synthesized insights from disparate disciplines like psychology and evolutionary biology to formulate a novel model of human decision-making.
Although the coalition members held disparate political convictions on economic policy, they stood united against the authoritarian dictator's constitutional revisions.
disparate.mnemonic: Disparate : éléments si différents qu'on ne peut pas les amalgamer.

disseminate.definition: To spread information, knowledge, or ideas widely
sentences: Public health agencies used social media platforms to disseminate accurate information about vaccine safety during the height of the epidemic.
The university library made digital archives publicly available to disseminate rare historical manuscripts to scholars across the entire globe.
disseminate.mnemonic: Semer (du latin semen, graine) : disperser des graines ou des idées partout.

distill.definition: To extract the essential meaning or most important aspects of something
sentences: The veteran editor managed to distill a dense six-hundred-page manuscript into a concise, punchy handbook that anyone could easily understand.
Great poets can distill complex human heartbreak into a single poignant stanza, expressing emotions that ordinary prose struggles to convey.
distill.mnemonic: Distiller : séparer l'essentiel du superflu, comme pour faire un élixir pur.

divergent.definition: Tending to be different or develop in different directions
sentences: The twin sisters developed strikingly divergent career ambitions, with one pursuing corporate finance in New York while the other taught literature abroad.
Negotiators struggled to reconcile divergent viewpoints regarding climate policy, as developing countries prioritized economic growth over strict emissions caps.
divergent.mnemonic: Diverger : prendre des directions opposées au lieu de converger.

diverse.definition: Showing a great deal of variety; very different
sentences: The national park boasts a diverse array of ecosystems, ranging from windswept alpine tundra to humid old-growth temperate rainforests.
Hiring candidates from diverse educational backgrounds helped the technology firm solve complex engineering challenges from multiple fresh perspectives.
diverse.mnemonic: Diversité : richesse de la variété et des différences.

divert.definition: To cause someone or something to change course or turn aside
sentences: Civil engineers built a concrete channel to divert floodwaters away from residential neighborhoods toward an uninhabited marshland basin.
The magician used flashy hand gestures to divert the audience's attention while secretly slipping the marked coin into his sleeve.
divert.mnemonic: Détourner de sa trajectoire ou distraire l'attention.

divisive.definition: Tending to cause disagreement or hostility between people
sentences: The politician's divisive campaign rhetoric deepened cultural hostility across the country, turning neighbors against one another over immigration policy.
School board meetings grew chaotic after parents began arguing over a divisive proposal to eliminate honors classes from high schools.
divisive.mnemonic: Divisif / clivant : qui coupe en deux et divise au lieu d'unir.

doctrine.definition: A belief or set of beliefs held and taught by a group
sentences: The military adopted a new tactical doctrine that prioritized drone reconnaissance and cyber warfare over traditional armored tank battalions.
Religious scholars debated the centuries-old theological doctrine, searching ancient scriptures to determine how historical councils had formulated the dogma.
doctrine.mnemonic: Une doctrine définit la ligne officielle d'une école de pensée ou d'une institution.

dubious.definition: Hesitating or doubting; not to be relied upon; suspect
sentences: Financial regulators grew suspicious of the bank's dubious accounting practices, suspecting that executives had concealed billions in bad loans.
Given the witness's long criminal history, jurors remained dubious about his testimony and demanded corroborating physical evidence before convicting.
dubious.mnemonic: Dubitatif / dubious : qui suscite le doute ou qui doute lui-même.

eccentric.definition: Unconventional and slightly strange in behavior or appearance
sentences: The eccentric inventor lived in a Victorian mansion cluttered with bizarre gadgets, refusing all telephone calls and communicating only via telegram.
While colleagues found her wardrobe eccentric, nobody questioned her brilliant mathematical intuition, which had solved several famous unsolved conjectures.
eccentric.mnemonic: Ex-centrique : qui s'écarte du centre de la norme.

eclipse.definition: To obscure the light from; to surpass or overshadow in importance
eclipse.definitionFr: éclipser, surpasser, reléguer au second plan
sentences: The young athlete's world record managed to eclipse the historic achievements of her legendary predecessor, stunning track fans worldwide.
Economic anxieties threatened to eclipse all other political issues during the election, dominating every debate and opinion editorial.
eclipse.mnemonic: Éclipser : faire de l'ombre à quelqu'un au point de le masquer complètement.

economical.definition: Giving good value or return in relation to the resources used
sentences: Commuting by bicycle proved far more economical than maintaining a car, saving the student thousands of dollars in gas and parking.
The novelist was famously economical with words, crafting spare prose that conveyed powerful emotional resonance through minimal description.
economical.mnemonic: Économe : qui gère sagement ses ressources (argent, mots, temps).

efficacious.definition: Successful in producing a desired or intended result; effective
sentences: Clinical trials demonstrated that the new antiviral therapy was remarkably efficacious in lowering hospitalization rates among high-risk patients.
Educators found that daily interactive reading exercises were far more efficacious than rote memorization for teaching vocabulary to young children.
efficacious.mnemonic: Efficace = efficacious : terme formel pour désigner une efficacité prouvée.

egoistic.definition: Excessively self-centered and preoccupied with one's own desires
sentences: His egoistic refusal to share project credit alienated fellow researchers, who eventually refused to collaborate on future grant proposals.
Psychologists described the executive as dangerously egoistic, noting that he treated corporate subordinates merely as instruments for his personal ambition.
egoistic.mnemonic: Ego = le moi : tourné exclusivement vers sa propre personne.

elaborate.definition: Involving many carefully arranged parts or details; complicated in design
sentences: The museum unveiled an elaborate mechanical clock from the seventeenth century that simulated the planetary orbits through dozens of interlocking gears.
Con artists devised an elaborate investment scheme to defraud wealthy retirees, fabricating convincing brochures and fake auditing reports.
elaborate.mnemonic: Élaboré : qui a nécessité un long travail de précision et de détail.

elitist.definition: Demonstrating snobbish superiority toward ordinary people; favoring an elite
sentences: Critics accused the private tennis club of holding elitist attitudes, pointing to its exorbitant membership fees and restrictive dress codes.
The professor rejected elitist arguments that classical literature was too difficult for working-class readers, establishing free public book clubs instead.
elitist.mnemonic: Élitiste : qui réserve l'accès à une petite caste privilégiée.

eloquent.definition: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing; clearly expressive
sentences: Her eloquent keynote address moved the diplomatic assembly to tears, making an impassioned case for immediate global climate cooperation.
The civil rights leader delivered an eloquent defense of human dignity that reverberated through newspapers and radio broadcasts across the globe.
eloquent.mnemonic: Éloquent : qui sait parler avec art, clarté et conviction.

embellish.definition: To make something more attractive by decoration, or more interesting by exaggeration
sentences: Grandpa loved to embellish his fishing tales, turning a tiny trout into a thrashing river monster that nearly sank his wooden canoe.
Medieval monks used gold leaf and vivid ink pigments to embellish the margins of illuminated biblical manuscripts with intricate floral patterns.
embellish.mnemonic: Embellir la vérité = enjoliver, broder des détails imaginaires.

emphatic.definition: Expressing something forcibly and clearly; striking or definite
sentences: The governor issued an emphatic denial regarding bribery rumors, swearing on television that he had never accepted improper campaign gifts.
With an emphatic victory in the championship finals, the underdog basketball team proved that disciplined teamwork could defeat celebrity talent.
emphatic.mnemonic: Emphatique en anglais = catégorique / énergique (affirmé avec force et certitude).

empirical.definition: Based on, concerned with, or verifiable by observation or experience
empirical.definitionFr: empirique, fondé sur l'expérience et l'observation
sentences: Rather than relying on abstract economic theories, the researchers gathered empirical evidence from fifty developing nations over three consecutive decades.
The scientific community rejected the miraculous health claim because its vocal proponents failed to provide any reproducible empirical test results.
empirical.mnemonic: Empirique : tiré du terrain et des faits réels, pas de pures théories.

enchant.definition: To fill someone with great delight; to put under a spell
sentences: The violinist's delicate performance managed to enchant the packed concert auditorium, leaving the audience breathless until the final chord faded.
Ancient folktales warned travelers that the singing forest nymphs could enchant unsuspecting wandering sailors and lure them into dangerous bogs.
enchant.mnemonic: Enchanter : charmer au point de donner l'impression d'un sortilège.

equitable.definition: Fair and impartial; treating all parties equally
sentences: Labor union representatives demanded an equitable distribution of company profits, arguing that workers deserved a fair share of the annual bonus pool.
The mediator helped the divorcing couple negotiate an equitable division of their marital assets without undergoing a bitter public trial.
equitable.mnemonic: Équitable = juste envers chacun selon ses mérites ou besoins.

erode.definition: To gradually wear away or deteriorate over time
sentences: Violent winter storms along the Atlantic coastline continue to erode sandy bluffs, threatening historic lighthouses built on the cliff edge.
Unchecked executive scandals and constant broken campaign promises began to erode ordinary citizens' trust in their nation's longstanding democratic institutions.
erode.mnemonic: Éroder : user petit à petit la roche ou la confiance.

erratic.definition: Not even or regular in pattern or movement; unpredictable
sentences: Because of erratic rainfall patterns caused by climate fluctuations, regional farmers struggled to determine the optimal planting date for their crops.
The police pulled over the driver after noticing his erratic swerving between highway lanes in the middle of torrential evening rain.
erratic.mnemonic: Erratique : qui erre sans trajectoire fixe ni régularité.

erroneous.definition: Wrong or incorrect; based on a mistaken assumption
sentences: Early astronomers based their planetary calculations on the erroneous assumption that the sun and stars revolved around a stationary earth.
The newspaper issued a prominent front-page correction after publishing erroneous financial figures that had unfairly damaged the candidate's public reputation.
erroneous.mnemonic: Erroné : plein d'erreurs (du latin errare, s'égarer).

escalate.definition: To increase rapidly in intensity, severity, or extent
sentences: Diplomats worked through the night to prevent the border skirmish from escalating into a full-scale regional war between the rival neighbors.
Failure to pay overdue utility bills will quickly escalate collection fees and could ultimately result in the permanent disconnection of service.
escalate.mnemonic: Escalade : monter les échelons vers un niveau de crise supérieur.

esteemed.definition: Held in great respect and admiration
sentences: The esteemed historian received a prestigious national award for his groundbreaking scholarship on civil rights struggles in the American South.
Medical students felt privileged to attend clinical rounds led by the esteemed neurosurgeon, whose innovative surgical techniques had saved countless lives.
esteemed.mnemonic: Estimé : jouissant d'une haute estime et d'une grande considération.

evasive.definition: Tending to avoid commitment or self-revelation, especially by responding indirectly
evasive.definitionFr: évasif, fuyant, qui élude la question
sentences: The corporate spokesperson gave evasive answers when pressed by reporters about upcoming factory layoffs, repeatedly deflecting to vague company talking points.
Detectives grew suspicious when the prime suspect gave evasive explanations regarding his whereabouts on the evening of the jewelry robbery.
evasive.mnemonic: Évasif : qui cherche à s'évader d'une réponse claire et directe.

evident.definition: Plain or obvious to the eye or mind; clearly apparent
sentences: Her deep fatigue was evident in the dark circles beneath her eyes and her slow, halting responses during the afternoon seminar.
It became immediately evident that the startup was struggling when several founding engineers announced their abrupt resignations on the same morning.
evident.mnemonic: Évident : qui saute aux yeux et ne requiert aucune démonstration.

evocative.definition: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind
evocative.definitionFr: évocateur, chargé d'émotion ou de souvenirs
sentences: The author's evocative descriptions of the seaside village filled readers with nostalgia for summers spent walking barefoot along windswept coastal dunes.
Hearing the evocative melody of the vintage waltz brought back vivid memories of her grandparents dancing in their candlelit living room.
evocative.mnemonic: Évocateur : qui réveille et évoque des souvenirs enfouis.

exacerbate.definition: To make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse
sentences: Cutting funding for public transportation will only exacerbate traffic congestion and worsen smog levels throughout the bustling metropolitan center.
Pouring salty water onto an open wound will only exacerbate the burning pain, making the injury far more agonizing to endure.
exacerbate.mnemonic: Ex-acerber = rendre acerbe ou acide : aggraver une situation déjà pénible.

exemplify.definition: To be a typical example of; to illustrate by giving an example
sentences: The humble physician seemed to exemplify genuine dedication, treating impoverished patients for free and working long past normal clinic hours.
Gothic cathedrals across northern France exemplify medieval engineering mastery, featuring soaring ribbed vaults and luminous stained glass rosette windows.
exemplify.mnemonic: Exemplifier : servir d'exemple parfait illustrant un principe.

exhaustive.definition: Examining, including, or considering all elements or aspects fully; comprehensive
sentences: After conducting an exhaustive investigation that spanned twelve months, detectives finally assembled enough forensic evidence to indict the corporate conspirators.
The doctoral dissertation presented an exhaustive review of published literature on renewable energy storage, citing more than six hundred academic journals.
exhaustive.mnemonic: Exhaustif : qui va jusqu'à épuiser le sujet sans rien omettre.

exotic.definition: Originating in or characteristic of a distant foreign country; striking or unusual
sentences: The botanic greenhouse housed exotic orchids collected from remote Indonesian rainforests, stunning weekend visitors with their vivid purple and scarlet petals.
Food lovers flocked to the neighborhood market to sample exotic spices and tropical fruits rarely found on traditional domestic supermarket shelves.
exotic.mnemonic: Exotique : qui vient du dehors (du grec exo, à l'extérieur).

expansive.definition: Covering a wide area in scope or size; friendly and open
sentences: From the mountain peak, hikers enjoyed an expansive panoramic view that stretched across pine forests to the distant snow-capped horizon.
After drinking several glasses of vintage champagne, the normally reserved CEO grew remarkably expansive, happily sharing anecdotes about his college pranks.
expansive.mnemonic: Expansif : qui s'étend largement dans l'espace ou qui exprime ses sentiments ouvertement.

explicit.definition: Stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion or doubt
sentences: The laboratory manual provided explicit instructions on handling volatile chemicals, warning students to wear safety goggles and rubber gloves at all times.
Contract negotiations broke down because the agreement lacked explicit definitions regarding which company would bear the financial costs of future shipping delays.
explicit.mnemonic: Explicite ≠ implicite : énoncé noir sur blanc sans sous-entendu.

exploit.definition: To make use of a situation or person, often unfairly or selfishly
exploit.definitionFr: exploiter, tirer profit de, abuser de
sentences: Sweatshop owners frequently exploit vulnerable immigrant laborers by paying below minimum wage and forcing them to endure hazardous working conditions.
The clever chess grandmaster was quick to exploit her opponent's tactical blunder, launching a devastating king-side offensive that forced immediate surrender.
exploit.mnemonic: Exploiter : tirer un avantage (parfois abusif) d'une opportunité ou d'une faiblesse.

fabricate.definition: To invent or concoct something, typically with deceitful intent; to construct
fabricate.definitionFr: fabriquer, forger de toutes pièces, inventer un mensonge
sentences: Desperate to cover up his gambling debts, the corrupt accountant began to fabricate invoices from fictitious consulting firms to siphon company funds.
Engineers used high-grade carbon fiber to fabricate lightweight aircraft components that could withstand extreme atmospheric pressures during supersonic flight.
fabricate.mnemonic: Fabriquer : construire du matériel, ou fabriquer un mensonge de toutes pièces.

feasible.definition: Possible to do easily or conveniently; plausible and practical
sentences: Urban planners determined that building an underground subway line was economically feasible, provided that national infrastructure grants covered half the construction costs.
Without adequate electrical grid capacity, relying entirely on solar power in northern winter climates is currently not a feasible technical solution.
feasible.mnemonic: Faisable = feasible : ce qui peut être facilement fait et réalisé dans la pratique.

feeble.definition: Lacking physical strength, especially as a result of age or illness; weak
sentences: After weeks of battling severe pneumonia in the hospital ward, the elderly patient was too feeble to walk without a nurse's support.
Critics mocked the politician's feeble excuse for missing the emergency climate debate, dismissing his claim of car trouble as childish nonsense.
feeble.mnemonic: Feeble = faible : sans vigueur physique ou argumentative.

feign.definition: To pretend to be affected by a feeling, state, or injury
sentences: Hoping to avoid Saturday morning football practice, the lazy boy decided to feign a severe stomachache until his sympathetic mother agreed.
Diplomats had to feign optimism during the televised peace conference, even though private communications revealed that peace negotiations had completely collapsed.
feign.mnemonic: Feindre : faire semblant, simuler une émotion ou un symptôme.

finite.definition: Having limits or bounds; not infinite
sentences: Environmental scientists remind us that fossil fuels are a finite resource, meaning that modern societies must rapidly transition toward renewable energy.
Because emergency medical supplies were finite, humanitarian doctors were forced to prioritize treating the most critically wounded earthquake survivors first.
finite.mnemonic: Fini : le contraire d'infini, qui a des bornes et des limites précises.

flamboyant.definition: Tending to attract attention because of exuberance, confidence, and stylishness
sentences: The rock star was legendary for his flamboyant stage outfits, which featured shimmering sequined capes, oversized sunglasses, and towering neon platform boots.
While the chef had a flamboyant personality on television, his traditional French bistro recipes adhered strictly to humble, classical culinary techniques.
flamboyant.mnemonic: Flamboyant : qui brille comme une flamme et attire tous les regards.

flourish.definition: To grow or develop in a healthy or vigorous way; to thrive
sentences: Under the patronage of enlightened merchant families, Renaissance art and philosophy began to flourish throughout Florence and across northern Italian city-states.
Desert cacti flourish in arid environments because their thick waxy stems store rainwater and minimize moisture loss during scorching summer months.
flourish.mnemonic: Fleurir / flourish : se développer vigoureusement et avec éclat.

fraudulent.definition: Obtained, done by, or involving deception or criminal fraud
sentences: Federal prosecutors charged the corrupt financier with orchestrating fraudulent investment schemes that robbed unsuspecting retirees of their hard-earned life savings.
The bank's cybersecurity software instantly flagged the transaction as fraudulent, freezing the account before overseas hackers could withdraw any stolen funds.
fraudulent.mnemonic: Frauduleux : qui relève de la fraude et de la tromperie délibérée.

frivolous.definition: Not having any serious purpose or value; carefree and superficial
sentences: The judge dismissed the lawsuit as completely frivolous, admonishing the plaintiff for wasting the court's valuable time on petty personal squabbles.
Instead of saving for his children's university tuition, the reckless lottery winner squandered his sudden fortune on frivolous luxury purchases.
frivolous.mnemonic: Frivole : léger, sans substance ni utilité sérieuse.

frugal.definition: Sparing or economical with regard to money or food; simple and plain
sentences: Through a frugal lifestyle of packing homemade lunches and buying second-hand furniture, she managed to pay off her student loans early.
The monastery monks ate a frugal dinner consisting only of coarse brown bread, vegetable broth, and fresh water from the courtyard well.
frugal.mnemonic: Frugal : sobre et modeste, ne dépensant que le strict nécessaire.

furtive.definition: Attempting to avoid notice or attention, typically because of guilt; stealthy
sentences: The student cast a furtive glance toward his classmate's examination paper, hoping the vigilant proctor would not notice his dishonest behavior.
The stray cat made a series of furtive movements along the dark alleyway, darting between garbage cans to evade the barking dog.
furtive.mnemonic: Furtif : qui passe comme une ombre sans se faire remarquer.

fusion.definition: The process or result of joining two or more things together into one
fusion.definitionFr: fusion, alliance, combinaison de plusieurs éléments
sentences: The restaurant earned international acclaim for its innovative fusion of Japanese sushi techniques with bold, spicy Mexican street food flavors.
Physicists around the world are working to harness nuclear fusion, hoping to generate clean, abundant energy without producing dangerous radioactive waste.
fusion.mnemonic: Fusion : réunion et mélange indissociable de plusieurs éléments.
